explanation: Keep one current value from every sorted array in an ordered collection. Measure maximum minus minimum, then advance the array contributing the minimum. Stop as soon as that array has no next value.
timeComplexity: O(N log k): at most N advances, each updating an ordered collection of k array heads. There is one maintained head per array and at most one advance per input entry.
spaceComplexity: O(k) heads and iterators, for k nonempty arrays. The heap or ordered collection holds one head per input array.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/minimum_distance_3_sorted_arrays.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Any better range than the current range must abandon a current minimum: increasing another head cannot reduce the maximum or raise this minimum. Advancing a minimum therefore discards no potential improvement. Once an array is exhausted, all further complete selections have already been dominated by a recorded range.
walkthrough: For [[1,7],[3,6],[4,8]], begin with (1,3,4), range 3. Advancing minima reaches (7,6,4), range 3, then (7,6,8), range 2. No smaller range is found, so return 2. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: The input may contain more than three sorted arrays.
Equal selected values can give range zero.
